text:
maria: Heads-up: nightly e2e perf gate turned red on longseq p95 and p99. Noticed surge around 03:10 UTC. CI shows ~2x p95 vs baseline.
sam: saw it too. Jenkins job  e2e-nightly-longseq (build 3221) failing the perf check step.
build-bot: [automated] e2e-nightly-longseq #3221 — FAILED — p95: 412ms (baseline 198ms), p99: 780ms (baseline 420ms)
li: output snippet from the runner logs:
```
2026-03-17T03:09:45Z runner: starting workload longseq
... warmup complete
step 1250: p95=410ms p99=772ms
KV cache hit rate 0.82
batch sizes: mostly 1-2
```
maria: KV hit rate looks fine. Could be scheduling noise or a kernel change. Any deployments around that window? ops-bot: no infra deploys in that window; autoscaler flapped briefly at 03:08 (scale +2 -> back down) due to a spike in queue depth.
tanvi: I pushed the small perf CLI change yesterday (PR #1892). It touched batching heuristics. @sam did you test longseq locally with that change?
sam: tested short runs, not full longseq. I'll kick a rerun and bisect if it repros.
li: suggest a quick triage: 1) rerun the same nightly job 2) run the short reproduce harness with PR tip and main commit 3) if repro, bisect range last 24h
maria: +1. If rerun is flaky, we should bisect to narrow down commit since we had a couple runtime tweaks in the last day.
sam: rerun queued: jenkins job e2e-nightly-longseq #3221-retry
build-bot: retriggered by sam at 03:12 — started #3221-r1
maria: tagging folks: @tanvi may have more context on the batching heuristics change, @li can help with KV cache telemetry.
tanvi: looking now. The change was gated behind feature flag and should have been off for nightly, but I see a flag flip in config service around 02:50 UTC. Investigating who toggled it.
ops-bot: config-service change by "deploy/batch-flags:enable-adaptive" at 2026-03-17T02:50:13Z by infra-automation
li: that matches window — if adaptive batching enabled, small-batch redistribution could bump latency for longseq that expects stable batching. Can we force flag off and rerun quickly?
maria: can we point the rerun at baseline (flag off) to confirm?
sam: rerun #3221-r2 started with override FLAG_ADAPTIVE_BATCHING=false
build-bot: #3221-r2 in progress
li: meanwhile I will run local harness: ./tools/longseq_repro --runs 5 --flag adaptive=false|true
tanvi: I can roll back the config flip if we confirm cause. But prefer verifying before rollback.
build-bot: #3221-r2 completed — PASS. p95: 204ms p99: 430ms
maria: that's promising. #3221-r1 (adaptive=true) was fail, #3221-r2 (adaptive=false) passed. Strong signal.
sam: running bisect plan: commit range from infra-automation config change + runtime commits in last 6 hours. But config flip seems the proximate cause.
li: local harness results: adaptive=true -> p95 median 408ms, adaptive=false -> p95 median 206ms. Repro'd locally.
tanvi: ok, I'm rolling the flag back to false in config-service and will add an audit note. infra-automation, please don't do automated toggles without the safe window :grimacing:
ops-bot: config-service rollback started by tanvi at 03:34:02Z — FLAG_ADAPTIVE_BATCHING=false
maria: thanks. Next steps: 1) keep flag off for 24h while we assess (tanvi) 2) open a follow-up to make adaptive batching opt-in per workload (maria) 3) add a smoke perf check in the flag flip workflow (sam)
sam: I'll open issue and assign myself to add the smoke perf job. Also will add a guard in infra automation to avoid flips during nightly window.
tanvi: created internal ticket PERF-847 to track fixes and rollout plan. Will also add a quick test that runs longseq subset when toggling batching flags.
li: adding KV/cache telemetry correlation graphs to the e2e dashboard to detect similar regressions earlier.
maria: great. Closing triage: root cause = config flip enabling adaptive batching. Immediate mitigation = rollback.
li: fyi I also captured flamegraphs from the failing run and attached to PERF-847.
maria: thanks everyone. If anything repros again ping here and we'll re-open. :thumbsup:
